newsitem.title: SPAIN: Madrid stocks lower on post-budget profit-taking.
newsitem.headline: Madrid stocks lower on post-budget profit-taking.

text.p: Madrid stocks closed lower on Friday as traders took profits after the government presented a draft 1997 budget broadly in line with market expectations.
The general index fell 1.31 points, 0.36 percent, to 366.45. The Ibex-35 leading share index lost 18.86 points, 0.45 percent, to 4,195.06.
Telefonica was down 30 pesetas to 2,370 with 4.6 million shares traded. Repsol gained 10 pesetas to 4,170 with volume of 1.2 million shares.
"It's normal that the market should recede a little after recent gains, but the mood is positive and we can regain a rising tendency during the next week," said a trader.
Trading volume remained firm, as in recent sessions, at 53.3 billion pesetas. Telefonica and electricity stocks were the most actively traded.
Large banks were mixed. BBV lost one percent while Banco Popular rose one percent after announcing an interim dividend of 183.75 pesetas.

Gas Natural was down 340 pesetas, 1.48 percent, to 22,600 after state holding company SETI approved the sale of the government's 3.8 stake in the energy group, as expected. Traders predicted the share price would be volatile in the short-term.
Endesa was unchanged at 7,550 and Iberdrola lost 15 pesetas to 1,250.
